subject: maths
title: Shapes, Direction and Movement - Faces, Corners and Turns
introductionText:
Term 3 · Geometry
Shapes, Direction and Movement —
Faces, Corners and Turns
The Big Idea: A shape keeps its name however you turn it. We describe shapes by their
sides, corners and faces.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"Hold this triangle. Turn it round. Is it still a triangle? Yes! It still has 3 sides and 3 corners.
Turning doesn't change a shape. A solid shape has faces — the flat parts you can put your
hand on. A cube has 6 faces and 8 corners. A cylinder has 2 flat faces and one curved face
that goes all the way round."
Watch Out For
The slip almost every child makes
Faces and sides mixed up. Sides belong to flat (2D) shapes; faces belong to solid (3D)
shapes. Let him press his palm flat on each face of a box as he counts.
Counting the same corner twice. Put a small sticker (or dot of play dough) on each corner
of a cube as he counts it.
Try It at Home
Game 1 — The feely bag (10 minutes)
Put a dice, a tin, an orange, a small box and an ice-cream cone (or funnel) in a pillowcase.
He feels one without looking and describes it: "It has flat faces... it has corners..." You
guess the shape. Then swap roles.
Game 2 — Playground spotting (a walk)
On the way to the park, find shapes: wheels are circles, a slide ladder has rectangles, a
football is a sphere, a traffic cone is a cone. Turn a road sign in your mind: is it still the
same shape upside down?
Turn it — still a triangle, still a square
corner
face
square still a square 6 faces, 8 corners
Turn the page round and ask if the triangles are still triangles. Then count the cube's faces on a real dice,
pressing each one.
More examples to talk about
• A sphere has one curved face and no corners.
• A cone has one flat face, one curved face and one pointy corner.
• A cuboid has 6 faces, like a cube, but some are rectangles.
• Tricky: a circle turned any amount looks exactly the same — try it with a plate.
• A sequence can use 3D shapes too: ball, box, box, ball, box, box...
Key Words
face corner side flat curved turn sequence forwards backwards

sourceQuestions.sourceText: How many faces does a cube have?
How many corners does a cube have?
Are these the same shape? Write yes or no.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Yes — both are triangles; one is just turned.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
Continue the sequence: sphere, cube, cube, sphere, cube, cube,
Name something in the playground that is shaped like a circle.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any circle: a wheel, a swing seat top, the top of a bin, a clock.

sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: curved: sphere, cylinder, cone • only flat: cube, cuboid, pyramid

sourceQuestions.sourceText: The robot faces up. Write the moves to get it to the star.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText:
2 forwards, turn right, 2 forwards. (Also correct: turn right, 2 forwards, turn left, 2
forwards.)

A shape that is turned round...
( changes its name ) ( disappears ) ( keeps its name )

A cone has...
( 4 corners ) ( 8 corners ) ( 1 pointy corner )

A sphere has...
( 3 sides ) ( one curved face ) ( 6 flat faces )

A cuboid has...
( 4 faces ) ( 2 faces ) ( 6 faces )

A triangle has...
( 3 sides ) ( no sides ) ( 4 sides )
